rationale: OQ-1 opening hours as request validation (400), no shift modelling — a static rule about the request cannot reintroduce check-then-act. OQ-2 service advisor, no auth — absent from the stated criteria and a solved problem. OQ-3 BOTH cancellation and rescheduling in scope, expanding on the architect's recommendation. OQ-4 retry remaining candidates then refuse — the candidate read stays advisory, correctness still comes from the insert. Quality-goal ranking ratified as proposed.

message: Record Gate A decisions as ADRs

rationale: ADR-0005 to ADR-0010 accepted as recommended, unmodified: Fastify+TypeBox, Kysely over pg with no ORM, node-pg-migrate running .sql files, five layered modules with no repository port, seeded-shuffle candidate ordering with a cap of 16, and GitHub Actions with check.run collected from the API rather than committed by the workflow. Three open rulings decided alongside them. (1) tests/architecture/ and tests/performance/ belong to the test-engineer, on the same reasoning as the other outside-in directories; CLAUDE.md section 5 and the path guard now carry it. (2) Slice 00 splits into 00a, a walking skeleton carrying compose, the first migration, /health and the phase-4 CI steps, before the pilot slice proper — so the pilot measures the loop rather than scaffolding friction. (3) TC-10 bites locally as well as in CI via .npmrc engine-strict=true. Separately, METHODOLOGY section 4 was corrected: it claimed the diagram-design skill scripts run in CI and they cannot, since they live outside the repository.

Scope and ordering approved as proposed. Thirteen slices, every arc42 section 10 quality scenario QS-1 to QS-14 claimed by the slice that makes it executable. Ordering driven by what must exist before the invariant can be tested rather than by feature value. The three contested seams stand: 00a/00 separating scaffold from invariant per the Gate B ruling, 02/04 so the retry loop arrives with a test that fails without it rather than as untested optimism, and 06/07 so the atomic move is separated from the two concurrency scenarios that catch a cancel-then-insert. Slice 07 is accepted as potentially proof-only, with the reviewer required to state explicitly if no production code changed.

reason: AC-6 reading resolved BROAD: "the acceptance suite failed" means any test-engineer-owned suite, not literally tests/acceptance/. Raised by the architect at step 2 as O-1 outcome (d): under the literal reading AC-6 is unsatisfiable for slices 07 and 11 (neither has a tests/acceptance/ file), and 00a own red commit trips it too by reddening both tests/acceptance/ and tests/architecture/. The fix under that reading would require changing an acceptance criterion, which CLAUDE.md section 6 forbids the architect. No acceptance criterion changes under the broad reading. Decided alongside: the slice arc42 scope gains 7.1, 11.2, 5.3 and 7.4; docker-compose starts postgres and otel-lgtm only with the service on the host, and 7.1/7.2 record the delta.

claim: The AC-4 fixture and lint:arch can both pass while examining nothing
scenario: Built the fixture to spec with four planted violations: depcruise exited 0, reported 0 violations, cruised 0 modules, because no typescript was resolvable. The negative control passes vacuously and lint:arch would report a clean architecture over an unexamined tree, so C4 reads a false green.

rationale: Finding upheld as (c). Remedy tightened: "resolves the real compiler" is not a mechanism, and totalCruised > 0 is the weak form — every planted file must appear in modules[].

claim: No acceptance test can start the service — no entrypoint, no loader, no owner
scenario: AC-1 and AC-2 both require a running service. The design names no start script, typecheck is --noEmit so nothing is emitted, tests/support/ has no owner and package.json scripts are unassigned.

rationale: Finding upheld as (a). Remedy rejected: no TypeScript loader — tsx is in no ADR and --experimental-strip-types does not remap .js specifiers. The project compiles instead, so the acceptance test spawns the artifact a deployment would run.

claim: The reasoning for implementer-authored tool tests is factually wrong
scenario: test:tools is a literal && chain of named files, not a glob, so a new tools/test/*.test.mjs does not run in CI until wired. Test-engineer-authored tool tests can therefore be red and invisible to verify, which also makes evidence item 3 independently authored.

rationale: Conceded outright: the stated reason was false and the conclusion does not survive it.

claim: red-proof's red zone makes slices 07 and 11 structurally unable to pass
scenario: The rule requires a failing file under tests/acceptance/. Slice 07 has only tests/concurrency/ and slice 11 only tests/performance/, so a correctly red commit exits 1. The negative condition is also stricter than AC-6, which constrains what must pass.

rationale: Finding upheld; the proposed remedy was REJECTED in part — excluding tests/integration/ would break slice 00, whose only test file lives there. Reading of AC-6 escalated to the human, who ruled BROAD: any test-engineer-owned suite.

claim: collect-ci's three constraints are correct but not sufficient
scenario: check.mjs:113 reads runs.at(-1) positionally while gh returns newest-first, so tests-green is judged on a stale run; and schema.mjs defaults ts to collection time, so collecting a red and a green run together makes C1 report FAIL on a correctly test-first slice.

rationale: Both agreed as constraints 4 and 5. The deeper fix to check.mjs declined: changing the gate tool in the slice that first feeds it is how you get a gate that agrees with its own bug.

claim: The design worked around a NON-NEGOTIABLE and called it a bootstrap paradox
scenario: CLAUDE.md §2.4 requires the red observed in CI; §7 offered four substitutes instead. METHODOLOGY:272 bars the board from leaving red until CI records the failure and :335 defines step 3 as logging that run, so the design produced an unloggable state, not merely weaker evidence.

rationale: Self-raised and self-ruled (c) on §2 authority. Fixed by landing the suite CI job in the red commit. Exposed a gap in §6 — the (c) test could not name a §2 invariant — since corrected in all three places the rule is stated.

claim: §7's predicted reason for AC-3's red is falsified by §4's own mkdirSync
scenario: globalSetup creates src/persistence/migrations before any test runs, so depcruise can open src and exits 0 over 18 modules. Two mechanisms specified in separate sections cancel each other.

rationale: Agreed; §4 and §7 both carried a false mechanism. The test-engineer's coverage assertion stands and is better than either mechanism.

claim: The lint:arch guard cannot detect an unexamined src/ — O1's failure mode inside O1's own remedy
scenario: The guard exits non-zero if no modules were cruised, but lint:arch cruises src tests and tests/ alone holds the count above zero. src/ goes unexamined behind a green gate and C4 reads a clean architecture.

rationale: Finding agreed; remedy refined — roots derived from argv, not hardcoded, and a single cruise, because outside-in-tests-do-not-import-src only fires when both roots share a graph. Prompted the general rule now in §5.

claim: The typescript pin is load-bearing and nothing warns if it is broken
scenario: npm i -D typescript installs 7.0.2; dependency-cruiser@18.2.0 supports >=2.0.0 <7.0.0 in src/meta.cjs, not peerDependencies, so there is no npm warning of any kind. Every cruise becomes inert and QS-10 switches off silently.

rationale: Agreed and made worse on the architect’s own check: the range is internal, so nothing warns at install time. Pin marked exact with the citation.

claim: collect-ci exports one mapper where constraint 4 needs a list-level export
scenario: Ascending order is a property of a list; with only toCheckRunRecord the ordering would live in the unexercised CLI and no test could reach it.

rationale: Agreed. Division of labour stated: per-run shape and ts in the singular, ordering in the plural, I/O and idempotence in the CLI.

claim: engines.node promises support the dependency tree refuses
scenario: The declared >=22.11.0 <25 admits 22.11, which vitest and testcontainers both reject, and 23.x, which vitest and dependency-cruiser both reject. CI is unaffected, so the only person who hits it is a developer the repository told was supported.

rationale: Agreed and found wrong twice rather than once. Corrected to >=22.22.0 <23 || >=24.0.0 <25; the numbers are the architect’s per arc42 §7.1, not TC-10’s.

claim: npm run typecheck is red at HEAD in a file the implementer may not edit
scenario: A false as ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams assertion; stdio ignore makes stdin null. Vitest transpiles without typechecking so the red commit never saw it, and green commit 9 puts typecheck on the verify job.

rationale: Fixed by declaring the overload’s real type. Emitted JS diffed identical, so the step-3 failure diagnosis is unchanged. Exposed that tsconfig.build.json excludes tests/, so pretest only looked like it typechecked the harness.

claim: §10's four-module prediction for graph:modules does not hold literally
scenario: mermaid output ignores reporterOptions.archi.collapsePattern, so the render is per-file inside directory subgraphs plus every node_modules package.

rationale: Agreed, cosmetic, gates nothing; recorded alongside the existing note that this render is to be eyeballed rather than trusted.

claim: judgeCruiseResult(summary, roots) cannot express the per-root rule it was ruled to enforce
scenario: Coverage needs modules[], a sibling of summary; a summary carries only totalCruised. And lint-arch.test.mjs passed bare summaries, so every committed case judged the F2 rule vacuously.

rationale: Finding agreed; remedy narrowed — a bare summary stays legitimate because three of four rules read only it, roots stays optional, and a missing modules[] gets its own distinct verdict.

claim: Repo-relative normalisation breaks the offline replay it exists to enable
scenario: Vitest records the runner’s absolute paths, so relative(cwd, name) yields ../../../home/runner/... matching neither the red zone nor the must-pass set. A genuinely red run replays as "no suite failed" — the discriminator reporting the opposite of what happened, on the one path that checks it.

rationale: Agreed; last-/tests/-segment fallback adopted and stated as a precondition of evidence item 3. Both alternatives recorded as rejected.

claim: gh exposes job display names, not workflow keys
scenario: The REST API does not expose the YAML key, so jobs.verify needs a name-to-key map; unmapped names must be slugified rather than dropped, or a failing job is invisible to constraint 2.

rationale: Agreed with two additions: a conformance assertion tying JOB_KEYS to verify.yml, and not-run failing closed against check.mjs:128.

claim: The layering guard can run the analyser it exists to guard against
scenario: The PATH fallback sits two lines below its own comment forbidding it. A global depcruise has its own node_modules and its own typescript resolution — the different-analyser scenario, minus the network.

rationale: Self-raised. Fallback becomes exit 2 naming npm ci as the fix, which makes the comment true.

claim: An assertion no correct collector could satisfy, unnoticed because the file was unwired
scenario: The green-then-red case fed the same two records in reversed array order, but check.mjs finds the failing run by regex and orders by timestamp, so array order cannot change the verdict. 29 of 30 passed and nothing ran the 30th.

rationale: Self-raised and fixed using the captured pre-slice green run rather than a third derived fixture. Produced the four-point discipline now applied to every assertion.

claim: repoRelative is not tested at all, and its fixtures encode a false belief about the tool
scenario: red-proof.test.mjs never imports failedFilesFrom, and its fixtures resolve against the local cwd so relative() always answers and the second branch never runs. §6 requires fixtures captured from the tool rather than encoding a belief about it; that was honoured for the gh payloads and not for the Vitest JSON.

rationale: Agreed and worse than stated. The red run’s real artifact is now a committed fixture; a relative()-only reader is shown to report "nothing failed" on the run that failed twice.

claim: Most of two CLIs carry rules that survive their own deletion with no test failing
scenario: lint-arch.mjs deliberately discards depcruise’s exit code because --output-type json exits 0 with violations present. Revert that and lint:arch goes green on every violation with nothing failing — the mutant prints the violation and exits 0.

rationale: Self-raised by the implementer when asked. All four named rules pinned, each watched failing against its mutant.

claim: The compiler diagnosis reports no compiler when one is installed
scenario: Three version reads shared one try, and dependency-cruiser’s exports map hides package.json, so a failure to read its version asserted that typescript was missing. It fires exactly when a developer has a working toolchain and a real violation.

rationale: Fixed by resolving package entry points and walking to the manifest, with per-fact failure isolation so a partial read yields a shorter true line.

claim: log:audit reports 12 false discrepancies because it assumes one agent.finish per transcript
scenario: A resumed agent stops once per resume, writing one agent.finish each, but all resumes share a single subagent transcript. The audit pairs records to transcripts one-to-one, so it reports UNSUPPORTED for every resume after the first and MISMATCH on duration because the transcript spans all of them. Slice 00a resumed the architect six times, so the audit now reports the honest record as untrustworthy — which is worse than not auditing, because C7 reads this output.

rationale: Real and mine, but out of scope for slice 00a: audit.mjs is orchestrator tooling and the fix is not a slice deliverable. Recorded rather than silently tolerated, because an audit that cries wolf twelve times is one nobody reads. Same root cause as the report-capture overwrite fixed in bdb32c1 — both tools were written assuming one spawn equals one run, and SendMessage resumes break that. Carried to the phase-4 retro under C7.
